title: Oscillating handoff mitigation via lightweight copy buffers and adaptive kernel hints
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Some production workloads show periodic host-side CPU spikes and memory-copy storms during prefill->decode handoff. These manifest as 99th-percentile latency spikes and increased variance in throughput for multi-tenant Dedicated pools. Root causes we see in traces: (1) frequent tiny pinned memcpy operations across many threads, (2) kernel-choice induced context switches when short sequences jump between small/large-kernel paths, (3) threadpool thrash due to imbalanced rendezvous work and per-request allocations.

Goal: Reduce observable host overhead (CPU p95/p99, memcpy storm amplitude, threadpool contention) without changing model semantics or increasing tail latency for cold requests. Target metrics: reduce host CPU p99 by >=30% for affected workloads, reduce memcpy micro-spikes by >=70% as measured by host memcpy histogram, and maintain or improve end-to-end p99 for generation traffic by at least 5 ms on average tests.

Scope: runtime repo + host-level scheduler and serving worker. This ticket covers design and prototype for a lightweight copy-buffer fabric combined with kernel-selection hints and a token-aware handoff that reduces per-request allocations and thread wakeups.
acceptance_criteria:
- New lightweight copy buffer allocator reduces number of host pinned memcpy calls per second by >= 60% in synthetic churn test.
- End-to-end p99 for prefill+decode workload decreases by >= 20% on our benchmark rig (NVIDIA H100; medium batch workload).
- No regression in correctness: outputs for regression prompt-suite match baseline within fuzz thresholds.
- Implementation behind feature flag with monitoring (memcpy histogram, thread wakeups, per-worker queue depth).
- Design doc + code review + perf dashboard showing before/after with clear test harness reproducibility steps.
design_notes:
Core ideas: 1) Lightweight per-worker ephemeral pinned buffers: allocate a small pool of reusable pinned buffers per IO-worker thread sized for typical prefills (e.g., 4-16KB slices) to avoid creating/destroying pinned allocations and reduce syscalls. 2) Rendezvous coalescer: introduce a microwindow (configurable, default 1-2ms) to aggregate adjacent small memcpy operations destined for the same GPU stream into one batched memcpy. Coalescer is token-aware: it prioritizes on-path tokens to reduce latency impact. 3) Kernel-selection hints: expose a minimal hinting API from scheduler to kernel selector with expected sequence-length distribution for the next microbatch so kernel selector prefers fewer context-switching kernels for mixed lengths. 4) Threadpool smoothing: use a lightweight slot-based admission (permits per worker) to avoid thundering herds waking multiple worker threads; backpressure is signaled to the frontdoor request router. 5) NUMA affinity hinting: when available, pin ephemeral pools to local NUMA node to avoid cross-node copies.

Trade-offs: small microwindow adds slight 1-2ms buffer for coalescing — must be token-aware to avoid increasing latency on interactive short queries. Reusable pinned buffers increase memory footprint slightly but should be bounded by worker count and slice size. Kernel hints are advisory; fallback to current selection if hint incompatible.
implementation_plan:
Phase 1 (Spiking):
- Build lightweight pinned buffer pool in runtime/io (feature-flagged).
- Add unit tests and stress harness that simulates high-churn small copy patterns.
- Add metrics for memcpy count, bytes coalesced, pool hit/miss.

Phase 2 (Coalescer + Admission):
- Implement rendezvous coalescer in IO-worker path with token-aware microwindow and correctness tests.
- Implement slot-based admission for worker threadpool and backpressure signal.

Phase 3 (Kernel hints + NUMA):
- Add minimal kernel-hint API between scheduler and kernel picker; plumb hint metadata through request context.
- Add NUMA-aware allocation path for pinned buffers and test on multi-socket perf rig.

Phase 4 (Canary + Observability):
- Enable feature flag on a small Dedicated pool; run synthetic and production shadow tests for 48-72h.
- Surface new histograms in console dashboard: memcpy_spikes, pool_miss_rate, worker_permit_wait_time, kernel_hint_mismatch_rate.

Rollout plan: behind feature flag; gradual ramp: 0% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% with gating on memcpy_spikes and p99 latency.

testing_plan:
- Unit tests for pool correctness and race conditions using sanitizer builds.
- Microbench harness that recreates small N=1..8 token prefill bursts across 64 workers to measure memcpy and thread wakeups.
- End-to-end perf tests against our H100 benchmark rig using same prompt-suite as ENG-93210.
- Shadow canary in Dedicated: deploy to 5% traffic with shadowing enabled to measure production-like variance.
- Perturbation tests: intentionally overload small-copy patterns to ensure admission prevents system collapse.
- Regression eval: ensure generation results within allowed numerical drift thresholds for eval set.
risks_and_mitigations:
- Risk: coalescing window causes latency regression for ultra-low-latency queries. Mitigation: token-aware bypass and per-endpoint flags to keep microwindow=0 for latency-critical services.
- Risk: pinned buffer leak or exhaustion. Mitigation: strict pool accounting, fallback path to on-demand allocation with circuit-breaker, and pool_max based on node memory.
- Risk: kernel-hint mismatch leads to suboptimal kernel choice. Mitigation: hints are advisory with telemetry; if mismatch_rate > 5% we disable hinting and roll back.
- Risk: NUMA path complexity increases code churn. Mitigation: keep NUMA allocator optional behind flag until stable.

notes:
Empirical observation: workloads with many short-turn interactive queries (median seq_len<=16) suffered most; batching heuristics previously optimized for throughput had unintentionally increased copy churn. This work aims to reconcile throughput heuristics with host-side cost efficiency.

If successful, this pattern (lightweight-per-worker-pools + coalescer + hinting) can be generalized to other I/O paths (KV cache warmups, embeddings hot paths).
